sights.n: Poké Lid — Emolga & Pikipek at Hinpun Gajumaru, Nago (ポケふた エモンガ×ツツケラ ひんぷんガジュマル)
sights.address: Gajumaru Ryokuchi Park, 2-321-3 Gusuku, Nago, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: A Pokémon manhole cover (Poké Lid) set beside Nago's Hinpun Gajumaru, the 240-plus-year-old national-monument banyan on Nago's main street. It shows Emolga and Pikipek playing in the tree. Nago installed it in Gajumaru Ryokuchi Park on 15 February 2022, and it is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.
sights.k: Pokémon manhole under Nago's great banyan
sights.anime: Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Emolga & Pikipek playing in the Hinpun Gajumaru, Nago's symbol; northern stop on the Okinawa Poké Lid trail

sights.n: Poké Lid — Wartortle & Sandygast, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (ポケふた カメール×スナバァ 道の駅いとまん)
sights.address: Michi-no-Eki Itoman (covered eating area), 4-19-1 Nishizaki-chō, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: A Pokémon manhole cover showing Wartortle and Sandygast on an Itoman sandy beach. It is set inside the covered eating area of Michi-no-Eki Itoman, the roadside station that houses the fishermen's co-op fish market. It is one of three south-Okinawa lids unveiled together for Itoman, Tomigusuku and Nanjō, and is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.
sights.k: Pokémon manhole at the fish-market roadside station
sights.anime: Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Wartortle with Sandygast on Itoman's beach; the southern-Okinawa Poké Lid set (Itoman/Tomigusuku/Nanjō)

sights.n: Poké Lid — Axew & Jangmo-o on a Hārī boat, Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki (ポケふた キバゴ×ジャラコ 道の駅豊崎)
sights.address: Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki, 3-39 Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Tomigusuku's Pokémon manhole cover shows Axew and Jangmo-o riding a dragon boat, a nod to the city's claim to be the birthplace of the Hārī boat race. It sits at Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki, the roadside station near Naha Airport. It was installed in the same south-Okinawa set as the Itoman and Nanjō lids, and is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.
sights.anime: Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Axew & Jangmo-o on a Hārī dragon boat, Tomigusuku's lid in the southern-Okinawa set

sights.n: Poké Lid — Growlithe, Zamami Village (ポケふた ガーディ 座間味村)
sights.address: 165 Zamami, Zamami Village, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: One of the four Growlithe Pokémon manhole covers the Pokémon Company gave Okinawan towns in 2025, alongside Chatan, Tokashiki and Kumejima. It shows Okinawa's 'support Pokémon' Growlithe in a Zamami island scene. The village gave its address as Zamami 165 and installed it in early August 2025. Ask at the Zamami Port visitor centre for the exact spot.
sights.anime: Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Growlithe, Okinawa's 'support Pokémon', in the 2025 four-town Growlithe set (Chatan/Tokashiki/Zamami/Kumejima)

sights.n: Poké Lid — Mantine & Remoraid, Ishigaki Port Remote Island Terminal (ポケふた マンタイン×テッポウオ 石垣港離島ターミナル)
sights.address: Near Euglena Ishigaki Port Remote Island Terminal, 1 Misaki-chō, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: The Yaeyama islands' first Pokémon manhole cover. It shows Mantine and Remoraid swimming in Ishigaki's blue sea, and was unveiled at Ishigaki City Hall on 11 March 2022 under the 'Flying Pikachu Project'. Trail write-ups place it near the ferry terminal you leave from for Taketomi and Iriomote, so it is easy to see before a boat.
sights.k: Pokémon manhole by the ferry terminal
sights.anime: Pokémon (Poké Lids / Flying Pikachu Project) — Mantine & Remoraid, Yaeyama's first Poké Lid

sights.n: Nishi-sanbashi West Pier, Taketomi Island (西桟橋)
sights.address: 207 Taketomi, Taketomi Town, Yaeyama District, Okinawa 907-1101, Japan
sights.w: A 105 m limestone-and-concrete pier built in 1938 on Taketomi's west coast. Islanders once sailed from here to farm rice paddies on Iriomote. It went out of use around 1971 and was registered as a Tangible Cultural Property in 2005. It is now the island's sunset spot, and it is the key-visual location of the film 'Non Non Biyori Vacation', which the Anime Tourism Association listed in its '88 Anime Pilgrimage Sites' from 2019 to 2024.
sights.k: Sunset pier and Non Non Biyori key visual
sights.anime: Non Non Biyori Vacation (2018 film) — the West Pier is the film's key visual; Anime Tourism 88 Yaeyama/Taketomi entry 2019–2024
